# Overview

The `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")` package provides a possible replacement
for `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")` workflows. It keeps familiar function
names and signatures while replacing the BioMart backend with the Ensembl REST
API.

`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")` is not (yet?) a complete implementation of the
BioMart query language. It currently supports a focused set of gene and
transcript annotation queries, sequence retrieval, and orthologue queries.
Interaction with non-Ensembl Marts should still be done with
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")`.

`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")` should not only be more stable, faster, but
also hopefully more user-friendly than `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")`, as
many arguments are no longer necessary. These arguments are silently accepted
for compatibility, but they are ignored.

All annotation and sequence examples in this vignette query live Ensembl
services. They require an internet connection, and results can change as Ensembl
releases and annotations are updated.

Although they are different approaches and interface, there is some overlap in
functionality between `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")` and 
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("ensembldb")`.
`EnsDb` objects from `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("ensembldb")`, available through 
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("AnnotationHub")`, give offline, release-pinned access to
gene, transcript and protein annotation, and they do not depend on the
availability of a web service at analysis time.

Beyond subjective preferences about interface, `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")`
is mainly useful when:

- existing code written against `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")` should keep
  working with minimal changes,
- orthologue queries are needed, through the Ensembl homology endpoint,

Finally, `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")` and `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("ensembldb")`
rely on different Ensembl APIs, which might have availability issues at 
different times. The option to use both packages in a complementary manner can
help mitigate such issues.

# Installation and loading

You can install remart from Bioconductor (after acceptance and release):

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false

BiocManager::install("remart")
```


The development version can be installed from GitHub with:

```{r}
#| label: install-github
#| eval: false

BiocManager::install("Huber-group-EMBL/remart")
```

Load the package in an R session with:

```{r}
#| label: load-package

library(remart)
```

Before anything else, we check if the Ensembl service is online using `is_ensembl_online()`:

```{r}
#| label: check-ensembl-online

ensembl_online <- is_ensembl_online(version = "may2024")
if (!ensembl_online) {
  message(
    "Ensembl service is currently offline.",
    "The remart queries in this vignette will not be executed."
  )
}
```

# Discover supported attributes

`listAttributes()` reports the attributes currently implemented by
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")`:

```{r}
#| label: list-attributes

listAttributes()
```

The supported filters for `getBM()` are currently limited to `ensembl_gene_id`, `ensembl_transcript_id` and `external_gene_name`, and only one filter can be used per call.

# Retrieve gene annotations

`getBM()` accepts the familiar `attributes`, `filters`, and `values` arguments.
The following query retrieves basic annotations for two human Ensembl genes. The
connection to Ensembl is handled internally, so a `mart` object is not required.

```{r}
#| label: gene-annotations
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

gene_ids <- c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939")

gene_annotations <- getBM(
  attributes = c(
    "ensembl_gene_id",
    "external_gene_name",
    "chromosome_name",
    "start_position",
    "end_position"
  ),
  filters = "ensembl_gene_id",
  values = gene_ids,
  version = "may2024"
)

head(gene_annotations)
```

Attributes are returned in the order requested. Duplicate identifiers are
handled internally, while identifiers that Ensembl cannot find are omitted with
a warning.

# Retrieve transcript-level annotations

Transcript-level attributes can be requested using gene identifiers. Because a
gene can have multiple transcripts, this may return multiple rows for one gene.

```{r}
#| label: transcript-annotations
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

transcript_annotations <- getBM(
  attributes = c(
    "ensembl_gene_id",
    "ensembl_transcript_id",
    "ensembl_peptide_id",
    "transcript_biotype"
  ),
  filters = "ensembl_gene_id",
  values = "ENSG00000157764",
  version = "may2024"
)

head(transcript_annotations)
```

Alternatively, transcript identifiers can be used as the filter when the query
is transcript-oriented:

```{r}
#| label: transcript-filter
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

getBM(
  attributes = c(
    "ensembl_transcript_id",
    "ensembl_gene_id",
    "ensembl_peptide_id"
  ),
  filters = "ensembl_transcript_id",
  values = "ENST00000357654",
  version = "may2024"
)
```

# Use the `getGene()` compatibility wrapper

For workflows written around `biomaRt::getGene()`, `getGene()` provides a
convenient gene-level interface:

```{r}
#| label: get-gene
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

getGene(
  id = c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939"),
  type = "ensembl_gene_id",
  version = "may2024"
)
```

The returned columns include `ensembl_gene_id`, `hgnc_symbol`, genomic
coordinates, strand, and description. Ensembl's REST response does not provide
the `band` field used by `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")`, so
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")` returns `band` as `NA` with a warning.

# Retrieve sequences

`getSequence()` retrieves sequences by Ensembl gene, transcript, or peptide
identifier.

For example, a cDNA sequence can be retrieved for a transcript as follows:

```{r}
#| label: cdna-sequence
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

cdna <- getSequence(
  seqType = "cdna",
  type = "ensembl_transcript_id",
  id = "ENST00000357654",
  version = "may2024"
)

summary(cdna)
```

Upstream and downstream bases can be requested for supported sequence queries:

```{r}
#| label: expanded-sequence
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

extended_cdna <- getSequence(
  seqType = "cdna",
  type = "ensembl_transcript_id",
  id = "ENST00000357654",
  upstream = 100,
  downstream = 100,
  version = "may2024"
)

summary(extended_cdna)
```

Coordinate-based requests using `chromosome`, `start`, and `end` are not yet
implemented.

# Find orthologues

`getLDS()` retains the familiar `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")` name, but its
current implementation is specifically for orthology queries through Ensembl's
homology endpoint. The target species is supplied with `speciesL`; this replaces
the linked `martL` connection used by `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")`.

The following example searches for mouse orthologues of a human gene:

```{r}
#| label: orthologues
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

orthologues <- getLDS(
  attributes = c("ensembl_gene_id", "external_gene_name"),
  filters = "ensembl_gene_id",
  values = "ENSG00000157764",
  attributesL = c("ensembl_gene_id", "external_gene_name"),
  speciesL = "mouse",
  version = "may2024"
)

orthologues
```

Only `ensembl_gene_id` and `external_gene_name` are currently supported as the source filter. Source and
target attributes are gene-level attributes; transcript-level linked queries are
not yet supported.

# Supported functionality

The table below summarises what each function supports. Filters, attributes and
`seqType` values not listed here are rejected with an error or, for arguments
passed through `...`, silently ignored.

| Function | Supported filters / `type` / `seqType` | Supported attributes | Differences from `biomaRt` | Not yet supported (and where to go instead) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `getBM()` | Filters (one at a time): `ensembl_gene_id`, `ensembl_transcript_id`, `external_gene_name` (requires `species`) | `ensembl_gene_id`, `ensembl_transcript_id`, `ensembl_peptide_id`, `external_gene_name`, `hgnc_symbol`, `description`, `chromosome_name`, `start_position`, `end_position`, `strand`, `gene_biotype`, `transcript_biotype`, `version` (see `listAttributes()`) | `mart` and other connection arguments are ignored; `species` replaces the species inferred from `mart`; `version` replaces the Ensembl release version inferred from `mart` | Multiple filters, other filters, and other attributes (e.g. external database IDs such as `entrezgene_id`). Use `biomaRt` for non-Ensembl marts or for these queries. |
| `getGene()` | `type = "ensembl_gene_id"` (default) or `"external_gene_name"` (requires `species`) | Fixed set: `ensembl_gene_id`, `hgnc_symbol`, `description`, `chromosome_name`, `band`, `strand`, `start_position`, `end_position` | `band` is always `NA` (not available from the REST API); `mart` is ignored; `species` and `version` are added | Other `biomaRt` identifier types and `band` values. Use `getBM()` for other attributes, or `biomaRt`. |
| `getSequence()` | `type`: `ensembl_gene_id`, `ensembl_transcript_id`, `ensembl_peptide_id`; `seqType`: `gene_exon_intron`, `cdna`, `peptide`; `upstream` / `downstream` in base pairs | Not applicable (returns sequences) | `chromosome`, `start` and `end` are not yet implemented (and throw an error) but are kept for positional compatibility; `mart`, `useCache` and `verbose` are ignored; `version` is added | Coordinate-based retrieval (`chromosome`, `start`, `end`). Use `biomaRt::getSequence()` for now. Non-Ensembl `type` values (e.g. `hgnc`, `refseq`) are not yet supported. |
| `getLDS()` | Source filters: `ensembl_gene_id`, `external_gene_name` (requires `species`); target filter `filtersL`: one gene-level attribute, or `""` | Gene-level attributes only, for both the source (`attributes`) and target (`attributesL`) species: `ensembl_gene_id`, `external_gene_name`, `hgnc_symbol`, `description`, `chromosome_name`, `start_position`, `end_position`, `strand`, `gene_biotype`, `transcript_biotype`, `version`. Transcript-level attributes (e.g. `ensembl_transcript_id`, `ensembl_peptide_id`) are not supported. | Orthologue queries only (Ensembl `homology/id`); the target species is given with `speciesL` instead of `martL`; `mart`, `martL`, `verbose`, `uniqueRows` and `bmHeader` are ignored | Transcript-level attributes, and general cross-database linking. Use `biomaRt::getLDS()` for these. |
| `listAttributes()` | Not applicable | Returns the attributes supported by `getBM()` and `getLDS()` | Takes no arguments | |

# Migrating common `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")` code

A typical `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")` workflow creates a connection before
calling `getBM()`:

```{r}
#| label: biomart-workflow
#| eval: false

# A biomaRt workflow.
# This example is not actually run as the biomart service is unstable.
gene_ids <- c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939")
attrs <- c(
  "ensembl_gene_id",
  "external_gene_name",
  "chromosome_name",
  "start_position",
  "end_position"
)
mart <- biomaRt::useEnsembl(
  "ensembl",
  dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl",
  version = 114
)
biomaRt::getBM(
  attributes = attrs,
  filters = "ensembl_gene_id",
  values = gene_ids,
  mart = mart
)
```

With `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("remart")`, the connection setup is removed and the
query can usually be adapted directly:

```{r}
#| label: remart-workflow
#| eval: !expr 'ensembl_online'

gene_ids <- c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939")
attrs <- c(
  "ensembl_gene_id",
  "external_gene_name",
  "chromosome_name",
  "start_position",
  "end_position"
)
getBM(
  attributes = attrs,
  filters = "ensembl_gene_id",
  values = gene_ids,
  version = 114
)
```

Several obsolete connection-related arguments are accepted through `...` for
source compatibility. Check `listAttributes()` and the function reference before
migrating a workflow that uses less common filters or attributes.

# Roadmap and future direction

We aim to implement additional filters and attributes, but we do not have full
visibility on how `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("biomaRt")` is currently used in
workflows in production. If you have a specific use case that is not currently
supported, please open an issue on GitHub.

## Known gaps

The items below summarize known gaps in `remart` functionality. Closing these gaps will depend on the availability of the corresponding endpoints in the Ensembl REST API, and priority as described below the table. "REST support" indicates whether the Ensembl REST API exposes what is
needed.

| Gap | Ensembl REST support | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple filters in `getBM()` | No single endpoint accepts arbitrary filter combinations. Requests are ID-based, so combining filters will need client-side filtering of results. | |
| External-ID conversion (e.g. `entrezgene_id`) | Yes, via the cross-reference endpoints (`xrefs/id`, `xrefs/symbol`). | |
| Coordinate-based `getSequence()` | Yes, via `sequence/region`. | |
| Transcript-level `getLDS()` | Partial. `homology/id` returns gene-level orthologues. Transcript-level attributes will need additional lookups. | |
| `listFilters()` | Not needed: the supported filters are fixed in `remart`, so the list can be returned locally. | [#17](https://github.com/Huber-group-EMBL/remart/issues/17) |

After initial release, feature development will be prioritized (in order) based on:

- Explicit feature requests from users in the [Bioconductor support forum](https://support.bioconductor.org/) and [GitHub issues](https://github.com/Huber-group-EMBL/remart/issues).
- Use cases in Bioconductor package currently using biomaRt, ordered by their number of monthly downloads.

# Understanding errors from remart

Beyond currently unsupported features, there may sometimes be a network or server-related error when querying the Ensembl REST API:

- HTTP 429: you have exceeded the rate limit for the Ensembl REST API. Please retry again after at least one hour. Rate limits are documented at <https://github.com/Ensembl/ensembl-rest/wiki/Rate-Limits>.
- HTTP 5XX, or timeout: the upstream server may be temporarily unavailable. Please retry the request after some time (next day if possible).
- HTTP 404: the requested resource could not be found on the Ensembl REST API. This may indicate an invalid ID or endpoint.
